State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Cloudtail India Pvt. Ltd. vs Daler Singh on 13 September, 2017
STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, PUNJAB,
 CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No. 35 of 2017

 Date of institution : 16.01.2017
 Date of decision : 13.09.2017

Cloudtail India Private Limited, having its Registered Office at

Ground Floor, Rear Portion, H-9, Block B-1, Mohan Cooperative

Industrial Area, Mathura Road, New Delhi-110 044, through its

Authorised Representative Komal Patwari.

 .......Appellant-Opposite Party No.1
 Versus

 1. Daler Singh s/o Gurucharan Singh, r/o 799, Basti Mithu, Near

 Baba Bachitar Singh Gurudwara, Jalandhar-144 002.

 .......Respondent No.1/Complainant

 2. Sehaj Tele Care, Ist Floor, Gulati Complex, Near DLF Mall,

 Nakodar Chowk, Jalandhar.

 ........Respondent No.2-Opposite Party No.2

 First Appeal against the order dated
 13.12.2016 of the District Consumer
 Disputes Redressal Forum, Jalandhar.
Quorum:-
 Hon'ble Mr. Justice Paramjeet Singh Dhaliwal, President
 Mrs. Kiran Sibal, Member
Present:-
For the appellant : Shri Nitin Thatai, Advocate.
 For respondent No.1: Ex parte.
For respondent No.2: Ex parte.
JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL, PRESIDENT:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant/opposite

party No.1 against the order dated 13.12.2016 passed by District

Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Jalandhar (in short, "the
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 2
District Forum"), whereby the complaint filed by Daler Singh,

respondent No.1/complainant, under
Section 12
of the Consumer

Protection Act, 1986 was partly accepted and opposite parties were

directed to repair the mobile set of the complainant and return the

same to him within 15 days from the date of receipt of copy of the

order. They were further directed to pay compensation of ₹5,000/-

for harassment and mental agony.
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties will

be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Forum.

Facts of the complaint:
3. Brief facts, as averred in the complaint, are that the

complainant purchased from opposite party No.1 one mobile (YU

YUPHORIA ON ANDROID, BUFFED STEEL) B015W4UQJS

bearing Serial No.911476050250620, vide Invoice dated 6.10.2015,

Ex. C-1, for a sum of ₹6,499/- including taxes. It is averred that after

some time the mobile phone started giving trouble. The complainant

contacted opposite party No.1-Company. Then the complainant was

informed to approach opposite party No.2, which is the Service

Centre of the Manufacturer-Company i.e. opposite party No.1.

Accordingly the complainant approached opposite party No.2 on

18.7.2016 and explained the problem; as a result of which opposite

party No.2 issued Job Card No.2122046-0716-24455337 dated

18.7.2016 and sent the mobile phone to the Company by making a

report regarding the problem i.e. "Power Switches Off". The

complainant thereafter visited opposite party No.2 i.e. Service Centre

on various dates and his mobile phone was received at Service
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 3
Centre on 9.8.2016. However, it did not work again. Opposite party

No.2-Service Centre again issued Job Card No.2122046-0816-

24844025 dated 9.8.2016. The complainant was assured that the

same will be repaired or replaced within 15 days but they did not do

anything upto 22nd of August 2016. The complainant continued to

remain in touch with opposite party No.2-Service Centre but no

response was given. The mobile phone was under warranty.

Despite repeated requests neither it was repaired nor replaced.

Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties, the

complainant filed the present complaint to provide him new mobile

phone in lieu of the previous mobile phone along with compensation

of ₹20,000/- for mental tension and harassment.
4. Notice was given to the opposite parties but despite service

opposite parties did not come present and were proceeded against

ex parte by the District Forum.
Finding of the District Forum:
5. In order to prove his case, the complainant tendered into

evidence his affidavit as Ex.CA and documents Ex.C-1 to Ex.C-3.

After going through the same and hearing the complainant in person,

the District Forum partly accepted the complaint, as stated above,

vide impugned order. Hence, this appeal.
6. We have heard learned counsel for appellant/opposite party

No.1 and have carefully gone through the records of the case,

including the affidavits of Mrs. Komal Patwari, Authorised Signatory

of appellant-opposite party No.1 tendered in the appeal by way of

leading additional evidence.
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 4
Contention of appellant/opposite party No.1:
7. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the

appellant/opposite party No.1 that the appellant/opposite party No.1

is merely the seller on the website and the Company, who

manufactured the mobile phone has not been impleaded as a party.

So appellant/opposite party No.1 is not responsible for payment and

repair of the same. The complaint is, thus, liable to be dismissed.

Consideration of Contentions:
8. We have given our thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the learned counsel for appellant/opposite party No.1.
9. Admittedly immediately after the purchase of mobile phone on

6.10.2015 it started giving problem and the same was brought to the

notice of opposite party No.1 from whom the complainant had

purchased the cell phone, vide Invoice Ex.C-1. The Job Card dated

18.7.2016 was given but after service, the cell phone was given to

the complainant on 9.8.2016. However, the same did not work

again. In fact, another Job Card No.2122046-0816-24844025 dated

9.8.2016 was given. Meaning thereby that when the cell phone was

handed over on 9.8.2016, it was not working at that particular point

of time. The complainant deposited the same with opposite party

No.2-Service Centre on the same very day. It was the duty of

opposite party No.1 to inform the manufacturer Company about the

defects in the mobile phone once the complainant had purchased

the mobile phone from it and should have claimed its rights from that

Company as that Company had not provided workable mobile phone

to the complainant. In these circumstances, though the
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 5
manufacturer-Company has not been impleaded as a party in the

present complaint but it becomes the duty of the dealer i.e. opposite

party No.1 from whom the complainant had purchased the mobile

phone to inform the manufacturer about the complaints of the

complainant. It is not the case of opposite party No.1 that they ever

made a complaint to the manufacturer from which they were/are

purchasing the mobile phones with regard to the defects in the

mobile phone of the complainant. In view of this, we are not satisfied

that the complaint should be dismissed on the ground of non-

impleadment of manufacturer-Company.
10. Since the purchase is from opposite party No.1 and the repair

was done by opposite party No.2, as advised by opposite party No.1,

therefore, opposite party No.1 is certainly liable for the same. In

view of this, we do not find any illegality or perversity in the

impugned order passed by the District Forum specifically when the

defect had occurred in the mobile phone within the warranty period.

However, it will be open to opposite party No.1-Dealer to claim its

rights from the manufacturer-Company from which it had purchased

the mobile phone. Moreover, opposite party No.1 has not annexed

any document on record from which Company it had purchased the

mobile phone nor made any application for impleading the

manufacturer-Company as a party before the District Forum or

before us. Certainly the complainant has suffered sufficiently for a

long period. So he is certainly entitled to the compensation so

awarded by the District Forum.
First Appeal No.35 of 2017 6
11. In view of our above discussion, we do not find any merit in the

present appeal and the same is hereby dismissed.
12. The appellant/opposite party No.1 had deposited a sum of

₹2,500/- at the time of filing of the appeal. This amount, along with

interest which has accrued thereon, if any, shall be remitted by the

registry to the District Forum, after the expiry of 45 days of the

sending of certified copy of the order to the parties. The complainant

may approach the District Forum for the release of the above

amount and the District Forum may pass the appropriate order in this

regard.
13. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory period

due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(JUSTICE PARAMJEET SINGH DHALIWAL)
 PRESIDENT

 (MRS. KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER
September 13, 2017
Bansal
